orch.title: Orchestration
orch.intro: A Claude Code pane pinned as orchestrator plans the work on the board and hands each task to a worker of its own, in a worktree. It decides how many workers run at once and how many times a task is tried. What is set here, Hangar holds itself, whatever the prompt says.

kitsManage.sectionHint: Enable the kits this workspace uses. Their skills, commands, agents and MCP servers load in its Claude Code panes.
kitsManage.sectionNone: No kit installed. Add one in Settings › Kits.
kitsManage.statusReviewHooks: To review: kept out of new panes
kitsManage.pendingNote: Enabled once the workspace is created. Setup commands run afterwards, from the workspace's "Kits…" menu.
kitsManage.actNothing: Nothing for Claude Code and no tab.
kitsManage.tabKindNativeFallback: Native, with an HTML page as a fallback
kitsManage.tabKindHint: A native tab is a WebAssembly module that Hangar draws itself. An HTML tab is a web page, shown in a window of its own. Both are held to the permissions below.
kitsManage.actNoSetup: No setup command for this system.
kitsManage.actSetupHint: Shown exactly as they will run, in a pane you can see, only when you click Run, once per machine.
kitsManage.actHooksHint: Claude Code runs these by itself, without asking, each time they match.
kitsManage.actHooksChanged: This list changed since it was accepted here, or was not shown in full then. Until you accept it, this kit stays out of the workspace's new panes.
kitsManage.actHooksLive: A linked folder is read live: what you change in this list applies without being asked again.
kitsManage.runModuleWhen: Claude Code loads this code into itself when a session starts: it runs inside Claude Code and sees what happens in the session. Hangar shows its path, not its code.
kitsManage.runMcpWhen: Claude Code starts each one, or connects to its address, when a session starts, and keeps it for the whole session. Claude can then call its tools.
kitsManage.runMonitorWhen: Each one starts in the background when a session starts, or the first time the skill it names runs, and stays until the session ends, with your rights and outside the sandbox. What it prints reaches Claude.
kitsManage.runLspWhen: Claude Code starts each one the first time Claude edits a file of the types shown, and it stays until the session ends.
kitsManage.runSkillHookWhen: While that skill or command is in use, Claude Code runs these by itself, without asking, each time they match.
kitsManage.runSettingsWhen: They apply when a session starts: agent makes the whole session answer as that agent of the plugin, and subagentStatusLine runs its command every few seconds while subagents work.
kitsManage.runGrammarWhen: Claude Code loads this JavaScript, from the plugin or from the address shown, to colour code in its interface.
kitsManage.runBin: Programs Claude can call by name
kitsManage.runBinWhen: Nothing starts these by itself: while the kit is on, Claude can run them by name from its shell.
kitsManage.runBinaryWhen: Claude Code may download these into bin/ when it installs the plugin, checked against this hash. Claude can then run them by name.
kitsManage.runDependencyWhen: Claude Code enables these along with this one, when they are installed, and they then run whatever they bring.
kitsManage.runUnknownWhen: Hangar does not know what these are. Claude Code may ignore them or, in another version, act on them: read them before you accept.
kitsManage.runUnreadable: Cannot be read by Hangar: what it runs is not shown here.
kitsManage.runEnv: Environment variables it sets (values not shown): {names}
kitsManage.stepOpened: Running in the pane {pane}. It is the visible pane of the workspace; close the Settings if they hide it. Hangar cannot read its exit code: once it ends, tell Hangar how it went.
kitsManage.stepNoPane: The workspace has no room for another pane.
kitsManage.stepPaneLost: The pane did not start in time, so it was closed and nothing was typed. Open the workspace, then run it again.
kitsManage.stepPaneLostDetached: The workspace is in a window of its own and its pane did not start in time. Nothing was typed. Open that window, then run it again.
kitsManage.actClaudeOnly: Kits reach Claude Code panes only, not the other agents or plain shells.
kitsManage.permWorkspaceRead: read this workspace's name and folder
kitsManage.permPanesRead: see your panes and when they change
kitsManage.permFilesRead: read text files inside the workspace folder
kitsManage.permDataRead: read the data this kit keeps in its own folder
kitsManage.permDataWrite: write data in this kit's own folder
kitsManage.permLoopback: talk to the local server on port {port}, and make it do whatever that server allows
kitsManage.warnHooks: Kit “{id}”: what it runs by itself changed, or was not shown in full, and is not accepted on this workspace, so the pane starts without it. Review it in the workspace's “Kits…” menu.
kitsManage.restartTitle: Running agents do not have it yet
kitsManage.restartBody: A Claude Code that is already running keeps the kits it started with. It gets {name} when it restarts.
kitsManage.everywhereHint: Accepted once, for every workspace, the ones you create later included. A workspace's own choice for this kit still wins.
kitsManage.everywhereReview: New permissions, or what it runs by itself, to accept: kept out of every pane until then.
kitsManage.everywhereNeedsWs: Open a workspace first to run this kit's setup steps.
kitsManage.everywhereOffNote: Turned off for all workspaces. The workspaces that enabled it themselves keep it.
kitsManage.everywhereRestartTitle: Running agents do not have the change yet
kitsManage.everywhereRestartBody: A Claude Code that is already running keeps the kits it started with. It follows the change for {name} when it restarts: restart the Claude Code panes of your workspaces.
kitsManage.everywhereToggleLocked: {name} is enabled on all workspaces: change it in Settings › Kits
kitsManage.galleryHint: The public kits of the hangar-ai organization on GitHub, listed by its catalog. Each is pinned to a tag: a new version reaches you only once the catalog names it. Installing brings a kit onto this machine: nothing runs and nothing is enabled. You see what a kit does, and accept it, when you enable it.
kitsManage.galleryEmpty: The library lists no kit yet. Kits show here once the catalog publishes them.
kitsManage.galleryCached: The library could not be read: showing the copy kept on {date}.
kitsManage.galleryUnavailable: The library cannot be reached, and no copy is kept yet. Check your connection, then refresh.
kitsManage.galleryCommunityNote: It was not reviewed by Hangar.
kitsManage.galleryInstalledFlash: {name} installed. It is not enabled: enable it on a workspace to see what it runs and accept it.
kitsTab.loadFailed: This kit's tab could not be loaded.
kitsTab.menuHint: Open a tab of this workspace's kits
kitsTab.menuNone: No kit enabled on this workspace has tabs.
kitsTab.isolatedHint: This page of the kit {kit} runs in a frame of its own: it reaches neither Hangar nor the network, only what the workspace granted it: {permissions}.
kitsTab.isolatedNothing: This page of the kit {kit} runs in a frame of its own: it reaches neither Hangar nor the network, and the workspace granted it nothing.
kitsTab.permission.panes.send: write to the Claude Code agents
kitsTab.permission.files.write: change the workspace's text files, hidden ones included
kitsTab.permission.loopback: talk to the local server on port {port}
kitsTab.permFilesWrite: change text files in your project, hidden ones like .env included
kitsTab.filesSecrets: This tab can both read and change your project's files, so it can also read hidden files such as .env, and the secrets they hold. Its page has no network of its own, but the kit's code can pass them on: to an agent with panes.send, and to whatever else the tab holds.
kitsTab.permCommand: run the command {name} on your computer, with your logins
kitsTab.commandsNone: No command: its tabs run nothing on your computer.
kitsTab.commandsChanged: These changed since they were accepted here. Until you accept them, this kit's tabs run none of them.
kitsTab.commandsLive: A linked folder is read live: what you change in these commands applies without being asked again.
kitsTab.commandHint: A tab of this kit can run this command on your computer whenever it wants, with your logins, for instance your gh login; only the parts in braces change, and they must match their rule.
kitsTab.commandHintFixed: A tab of this kit can run this command on your computer whenever it wants, with your logins, for instance your gh login; nothing in it changes.
kitsTab.commandKitDir: {kitDir} is this kit's own folder, which Hangar fills in: this command runs a script of the kit. You see its name here, not what it does, and an update can change that without asking again.
kitsTab.everywhereReviewCommands: Changed commands to accept: this kit's tabs run none of them until then.
kitsTab.disabled: This kit is no longer enabled on this workspace.
kitsTab.disabledHint: Enable it again on the workspace to use this tab.
kitsTab.missing: This tab is no longer in an installed kit.
kitsTab.missingHint: The kit was removed, or an update took this tab out of it.
kitsTab.broken: This kit cannot be used right now.
kitsTab.leftHint: A kit's tab only speaks to Hangar from the page it opened on, so the page it went to was closed. Reload the tab to start again.
kitsTab.windowHint: A browser engine draws this kit's page, in a window of its own, so that it stays apart from Hangar.
kitsTab.nativeIsolatedHint: This tab of the kit {kit} runs sealed off: it reaches neither Hangar nor the network, only what the workspace granted it: {permissions}.
kitsTab.nativeIsolatedNothing: This tab of the kit {kit} runs sealed off: it reaches neither Hangar nor the network, and the workspace granted it nothing.
kitsTab.native.newer: A part of this tab needs a newer Hangar.
kitsTab.native.imageTooLarge: This image is larger than 10 MB
kitsTab.fallbackHint: This Hangar could not load the tab's module, so it shows the kit's page instead: {reason}
worktrees.cleanupHint: Removes, in one go, the worktrees whose branch is already merged
worktrees.cleanupIntro: These worktrees sit on a branch already merged into the main checkout. The ones that look finished are ticked.
worktrees.cleanupNone: No worktree sits on a merged branch.
worktrees.cleanupNoOwnCommitHint: Its branch is at the same commit as the main checkout, so git counts it as merged — it may be a worker that has just started
worktrees.cleanupHeldHint: A pane of Hangar is open in this worktree
worktrees.cleanupLockedHint: Locked: unlock it first to remove it
worktrees.cleanupConfirmDirty: {n} of them hold uncommitted work: git will refuse to remove them, and you will be asked again for each.
worktrees.cleanupNeedsForce: Held back by git — force removes what they hold:
worktrees.cleanupBranches: Their branches are merged and no worktree holds them any more. Delete them?
worktrees.migrateHint: Moves this worktree's uncommitted changes into the main checkout
worktrees.migrateWarn: This empties the uncommitted changes of this worktree and applies them in the main checkout. Staged files come across as plain changes.
worktrees.migrateDone: Changes brought back to the main checkout.
worktrees.migrateNothing: This worktree has no uncommitted change.
worktrees.migrateConflict: Modified both here and in the main checkout, nothing was moved:
worktrees.migrateFailed: The changes could not be applied in the main checkout. Nothing is lost: they are kept in a stash. Get them back with: git stash apply {stash}
worktrees.migrateDropFailed: Changes brought back, but their stash could not be dropped. It is harmless; remove it with git stash drop when you want.
worktrees.hooksRunsHere: These commands run on this machine, as you, through your default shell. Only you can set them: no agent can.
worktrees.hooksPostCreateHint: Runs in the new worktree, for the panel's and for a worker's, with WORKTREE_PATH and BASE_PATH set. If it fails the worktree is kept and the failure is shown (and told to the worker).
worktrees.hooksPreRemoveHint: Runs in the worktree first, also when cleaning up merged ones. If it fails or runs past 5 minutes the worktree is kept, and you can remove it anyway.
worktrees.hooksPlaceholder: Empty runs nothing — e.g. pnpm install
worktrees.hookPostFailed: The postCreate command {problem}. The worktree was kept.
gitConsent.title: {by} wants to clone a repository
gitConsent.titleUnknown: An agent wants to clone a repository
gitConsent.warning: Installing its dependencies runs its code on this machine. Its orchestrator tells you what the install would run before it installs anything.
gitConsent.logAllow: Clone of {repo} into the folder "{folder}": you clicked Clone
gitConsent.logRefuse: Clone of {repo} into the folder "{folder}": you clicked Refuse
gitConsent.logTimeout: Clone of {repo} into the folder "{folder}": no answer in time, nothing cloned
create.gitRepoPlaceholder: owner/repo, or an https or ssh address
create.gitParentHint: empty: the Projects folder from the settings, else next to the current workspace
create.gitNoFolder: There is no folder to clone into: pick one
create.gitReused: {path} already held this repository: it was used as it was
create.gitExisting: A workspace is already on {path}: it is shown
settings.projectsFolderHint: Where repositories cloned from Git go. Empty: next to the current workspace's folder
paneBranch.branchWorktree: Git branch {branch}, in a linked worktree
accounts.settings.title: Claude accounts
accounts.settings.intro: Each account is a separate Claude subscription. Choose one per workspace; Hangar never switches on its own when a limit is reached.
accounts.settings.removeBody: Its login is deleted from this computer. Workspaces on it go back to the default account.
accounts.settings.mainFixed: The main account is Claude Code’s own configuration: it cannot be removed.
accounts.settings.addHint: A pane opens so you can log in through your browser.
accounts.settings.nameTaken: Another account already has this name.
accounts.settings.unsupportedTitle: Logins are not kept apart on this computer
accounts.settings.unsupportedBody: Logging in to one account here may log another one out. You may have to log in again after switching.
accounts.settings.noPane: No room for the login pane. Close a pane in the open workspace, then choose “Log in” on the account.
accounts.switcher.heading: This workspace uses
accounts.switcher.useEverywhereLabel: Make {name} the default for every workspace
accounts.switcher.askEverywhere: Make {name} the default for every workspace
accounts.switcher.restartHere: Restart this workspace’s agents now (conversations kept)
accounts.switcher.restartEverywhere: Restart the agents that follow the default now (conversations kept)
accounts.picker.label: Claude account
accounts.picker.missing: The account “{id}” no longer exists: the default applies.
accounts.badge.title: Claude account: {name}
accounts.menu.title: Claude account
accounts.pane.badgeTitle: This agent runs on the “{name}” account, not its workspace’s
